parameters.prompt:
You are the incident analyst for ${trigger.incident_id}: PHP2Shell (${trigger.cves}), advisory ${trigger.advisory}.

The classification below was produced by REVIEWED, DETERMINISTIC automation and is shown on screen next to your text. Do not change any priority, action or fix status. Your job is to explain it for the CISO and for service owners.

Classification (priority / service / SAPI / exposure / action / installed / fixed in):
${know_scan.artifacts.p2s_table}

Log look-back ("were we already hit?"): ${know_lookback.artifacts.p2s_lookback_text}

Rules:
- Use only the facts above. If something is not in the evidence, say it is unknown.
- In "unknowns", write each unknown asset exactly as: "<service>: no evidence collected; listed exposure <exposure from the table>". Add nothing else to "unknowns".
- Do NOT state version numbers, package names or advisory ids; the table is authoritative for those.
- Nothing has been changed yet: describe actions as planned (to contain, to isolate), never as done.
- Never describe any asset as "safe" or "protected". Unreachable assets are UNKNOWN, not clear.
- A look-back hit is a signal for forensic triage, not proof of compromise.
- Describe a look-back hit only as what the evidence shows (for example: one probe-shaped request logged, sent to forensic triage). Never write that an exploit, attack or compromise was detected, confirmed or happened.
- Triage and every other action are planned, not started: never write that anything is in progress or already done.
- Write the look-back hit as "sent to forensic triage". Never write "under triage", "being triaged" or "initiated".
- Be brief and concrete; name services, not hostnames.

Return only one JSON object that matches this JSON schema, with no other text before or after it:
{"properties":{"are_we_affected":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"exec_summary":{"description":"<= 60 words for the CISO","minLength":1,"type":"string"},"forensic_triage":{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"},"unknowns":{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"},"were_we_hit":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}},"required":["exec_summary","are_we_affected","were_we_hit","unknowns"],"type":"object"}

parameters.prompt:
Extract the interim mitigation for PHP2Shell using ONLY the recorded advisory text between the BEGIN and END markers at the end of this prompt: verbatim mitigation sections of Red Hat bulletin RHSB-2026-013 and of the php.net notice. Do not use any other knowledge; if the documents do not say it, do not include it.

In-scope stacks: RHEL 10 php-fpm services and a php:8.4 Apache (mod_php) container. Business context: payments-portal, customer-api and partner-portal accept invoice uploads (max 2 MB). marketing-site does not accept uploads.

Return:
- settings: php.ini-level settings for which the documents give a LITERAL value (for example 0, -1, 32M), each with a citation (document + section heading) and a verbatim quote of at most 25 words. Choose values appropriate for services that accept uploads where the advisory distinguishes. A directive the documents describe only as a condition or relationship (for example "below post_max_size") must NOT appear in settings: state that relationship in requires instead. Never write a sentence in a value. List each setting once, with the single value for the upload services. Include only directives that exist in PHP 8.3 and PHP 8.4, the in-scope versions: if a section of the documents applies only to other PHP versions or other products, leave its settings out of settings and mention them in cautions.
- requires: prerequisites the automation must enforce or verify for these settings to be valid (as stated in the documents).
- residual_risk_quote: the advisory's own verbatim sentence on whether configuration changes substitute for patching.
- cautions: business-impact warnings stated in the documents.

----- BEGIN RECORDED ADVISORY (sha256 5e976af9a5b70ca79ade5367f0d40b1c56e84e515b507d71af0464bf18203db4) -----
RECORDED ADVISORY EXCERPT for PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619). Verbatim spans, nothing paraphrased.
Span 1: RHSB-2026-013.snapshot.txt (sha256 856f806b38edc18145cd0f59bf1911159514d0c0a05ff329475cf946ebb6dbdd), from heading 'Mitigation' up to 'Acknowledgements'.
Span 2: php.net-2026-10-21.snapshot.txt (sha256 bafcd8831586056fa65c0dbec0758b4d58d47123f0215b6f3b9122328e0c04c8), the paragraph beginning 'If you cannot update immediately'.

===== SPAN 1: Red Hat Security Bulletin RHSB-2026-013 =====
Mitigation

Overall Guidance

Configuration changes can prevent the vulnerable paths from being reached, but they may disrupt workloads and are not a substitute for patching. Disabling session upload progress fully protects against CVE-2026-115560, and removes exposure to CVE-2026-109619 on the php package shipped with Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, but on other products it blocks only the confirmed session paths. The memory limit and request size changes remove the attacker-controllable failure for CVE-2026-109618 but do not eliminate it, because an underlying allocation failure can still reach the affected code. Patching is the only comprehensive solution that both fixes the vulnerabilities and maintains full functionality.

The PHP project publishes additional application-level hardening guidance in its upstream advisories, linked in the References section below.

Product-Specific Mitigation Steps

Apply all settings below using php_admin_value in the PHP-FPM pool or Apache HTTP Server configuration so that applications cannot override them. Settings must take effect before request parsing begins, so ini_set() and PHP-FPM .user.ini files are not suitable.

Restart every worker after any change. A reload is not sufficient, because existing workers may retain affected state from earlier requests.

systemctl restart httpd      # mod_php, the default on RHEL 7
systemctl restart php-fpm    # PHP-FPM, the default on RHEL 8 and later

In containerized deployments, replace the running container or pod.

Disable Session Upload Progress

Addresses CVE-2026-109619 and CVE-2026-115560. This is the single most effective change and the only one required on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7.

Warning: Applications using PHP's native session upload-progress reporting will no longer receive progress data. Applications that report upload progress in the browser are unaffected.

session.upload_progress.enabled = 0

This directive is commented out in the shipped /etc/php.ini and defaults to enabled, so the line must be added and set to 0. Uncommenting the shipped line leaves the feature enabled.

Audit for .htaccess, virtual host php_value, and .user.ini settings that could re-enable it per directory. Using php_admin_value prevents these overrides. Verify through a temporary phpinfo() page rather than php -i, which reports the command-line configuration.

CVE-2026-115560 affects only applications that set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime are not exposed to that flaw. This setting remains recommended regardless, as it also addresses CVE-2026-109619.

Keep this setting in place until the updates are applied. For CVE-2026-115560 alone, upstream expects a fix in the next routine PHP release.

Remove the Controllable Memory Limit

Addresses CVE-2026-109618. Not required on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 7, which is not affected by this flaw.

Warning: This removes PHP's own memory ceiling. Do not apply it without an external availability boundary in place, or a single runaway request can exhaust system memory.

memory_limit = -1

Verify that no pool, directory, or application setting reimposes a finite limit. Impose the availability boundary with a container or cgroup limit instead, preferably with a policy that terminates only the affected worker.

Warning: Do not use RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA for this purpose. They produce exactly the allocation failure that reaches the affected code and will make the problem worse.

Limit Request Size

Addresses CVE-2026-109618.

Warning: Applications accepting large uploads or large form posts will break if the limit is set below what they require. Review current values before applying.

post_max_size = 8M     # applications that do not require file uploads
post_max_size = 32M    # applications that require file uploads

Keep upload_max_filesize below post_max_size. Consider enforcing further limits at the web server or proxy for decoded request size, input field count, multipart part count, header count, and nesting depth. These must also apply to requests without a usable Content-Length header.

Additional Steps for PHP 8.5

Addresses the confirmed fatal error backtrace path for CVE-2026-109619. The setting does not exist on earlier PHP versions. Of the products listed above, this applies to Red Hat Hardened Images.

Warning: Fatal error backtraces will no longer be recorded, which may hinder application debugging.

fatal_error_backtraces = 0

===== SPAN 2: php.net security notice (21 Oct 2026) =====
If you cannot update immediately: while only an update is a complete solution, the following measures reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe.

----- END RECORDED ADVISORY -----

Return only one JSON object that matches this JSON schema, with no other text before or after it:
{"properties":{"cautions":{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"},"requires":{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"},"residual_risk_quote":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"settings":{"items":{"properties":{"citation":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"quote":{"type":"string"},"setting":{"minLength":1,"type":"string"},"value":{"description":"literal php.ini value only, e.g. 0, -1, 32M","minLength":1,"pattern":"^-?[0-9]+[KMGkmg]?$","type":"string"}},"required":["setting","value","citation"],"type":"object"},"type":"array"}},"required":["settings","requires","residual_risk_quote"],"type":"object"}

parameters.prompt:
SERVICE OWNER DECISION - payments-portal (team-payments) - ${trigger.incident_id}

payments-portal runs PHP under mod_php and is internet-facing: the highest-risk configuration for PHP2Shell.
To contain it, the edge will reject multipart uploads. Invoice upload on payments-portal will be UNAVAILABLE until the fixed image (php 8.4.27) is deployed.

Exception window: 72 hours from approval. At expiry the incident commander must re-approve or escalate.

APPROVE = accept the upload outage as the price of containment.
REJECT = keep uploads; the residual risk is recorded against payments-portal.
